tools.name: find_files
tools.description: Fuzzy-find files by path in a folder, best match first. Respects .gitignore. Returns each file's path, score and the matched character ranges. `path` must be a folder.

query.description: Part of a file name or path, e.g. `mcp tools`

path.description: The folder to search, an absolute path (e.g. the repo's root); the working directory when omitted. Not a file

folder.description: The older name of `path`, still taken; pass one of the two (both, if different, is invalid)

git.description: Rank files with uncommitted changes and recently committed files higher, the way an editor's quick-open does; default false

tools.name: search_text
tools.description: Search the contents of a folder's files, or of one file, with ripgrep. Respects .gitignore; skips hidden and binary files. Returns each matching file with all its matching lines (1-based) and match ranges, up to `limit` files and `max_lines` lines in total; `truncated` marks where the search stopped.

query.description: A literal string, or a regex when `regex` is true

path.description: The folder to search, or one file to search alone, an absolute path (e.g. the repo's root); the working directory when omitted. A file's matches are answered under its name

folder.description: The older name of `path`, still taken; pass one of the two (both, if different, is invalid)

globs.description: ripgrep globs limiting the files; a leading `!` excludes

limit.description: Files returned, each with all its matching lines, up to `max_lines` lines in total; default 50

max_lines.description: Matching lines returned in total, over all files; default 2000. The file that reaches it is marked `truncated`

tools.name: search_structural
tools.description: Search a folder's code, or one file, by syntax with an ast-grep pattern. Respects .gitignore. Returns each matching file with all its matching lines and match ranges, as search_text does, up to `limit` files and `max_lines` lines in total. A pattern is code with metavariables: `$A` matches one node, `$$$A` any number. Examples: TS/JS: `console.log($A)`, `function $F($$$A) { $$$B }`, `$P.then($F)`; Python: `def $F($$$A): $$$B`, `class $C: $$$B`, `print($$$A)`; Rust: `fn $N($$$A) { $$$B }`, `let $V = $E.unwrap();`, `println!($$$A)`; Go: `func $F($$$A) { $$$B }`, `func ($R $T) $M($$$A) { $$$B }`, `type $T struct { $$$F }`. A declaration needs its body: a pattern that does not parse, like `def $F($$$A)`, `fn $N($$$A)` or `impl $T for $U`, is run once more with the body added, and the answer's `note` says so and names what that pattern skips (a return type, `pub`, ...).

pattern.description: An ast-grep pattern; `$A` matches one node

path.description: The folder to search, or one file to search alone, an absolute path (e.g. the repo's root); the working directory when omitted. A file's matches are answered under its name

folder.description: The older name of `path`, still taken; pass one of the two (both, if different, is invalid)

lang.description: The pattern's language; each file's own, from its extension, when omitted

globs.description: ripgrep globs limiting the files; a leading `!` excludes

limit.description: Files returned, each with all its matching lines, up to `max_lines` lines in total; default 50

max_lines.description: Matching lines returned in total, over all files; default 2000. The file that reaches it is marked `truncated`

note.description: Set only when the pattern was run with a body added: which pattern was searched, and what that one skips, e.g. "searched `def $F($$$A): $$$BODY` (added the body the pattern needs; it skips defs with a return annotation; to match those, add `-> $R` before the colon)"

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: Every file in a folder that ripgrep would search: .gitignore respected, hidden files skipped. Paths in no particular order; `truncated` when cut at the limit. `path` must be a folder.

path.description: The folder to search, an absolute path (e.g. the repo's root); the working directory when omitted. Not a file

folder.description: The older name of `path`, still taken; pass one of the two (both, if different, is invalid)

tools.name: search_sessions
tools.description: Search this machine's Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode conversations for a phrase in what was said (prompts, answers, tool calls and output), newest first. Returns each session's harness, id, title, last write and up to 3 matching snippets.

query.description: A literal phrase, not a regex

path.description: Only sessions run in this folder (an absolute path, e.g. the repo's root); every folder's when omitted. Not a file

folder.description: The older name of `path`, still taken; pass one of the two (both, if different, is invalid)
